items.headline: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation threat, Air Force says
items.blurb: Hours later Russian authorities said its app was also hacked, with fake warnings sent inside the country.
items.text: Ukraine's air raid alert app was apparently hacked on Sunday and for a short time said the capital Kyiv was subject to a radiation threat, the Ukrainian Air Force has said. The alert on Telegram read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel." The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said there had been a failure in the app, and urged people to use other sources of information to clarify the situation on the threat of air strikes. A few hours later Russian authorities said its app was hacked. A Ukrainian espionage group claimed fake warnings of nuclear strikes inside Russia had been sent to users. Russia has the world's biggest nuclear arsenal, and President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly suggested an openness to using all weapons at Russia's disposal . The alerts, in Ukrainian, started at approximately 22:47 (20:47 GMT), with red-level air raids apparently issued nationwide. Additional warnings were issued in Kyiv, with the first reading: "Radiation threat. Radiation threat declared in Kyiv."

items.headline: Ukraine blames Russia after air alert app sends out false warnings
items.blurb: Russian Emergencies Ministry also says its mobile app suffered a 'massive cyberattack', leading to 'false information'.
items.text: Ukraine’s Air Force has said its air raid alert app sent erroneous messages after allegedly being hacked by Russia. Fake alerts warning of nuclear and chemical threats to areas in and around Kyiv were sent on Sunday, along with warnings of potential street combat. An erroneous message also said Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed. “The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian Air Force said on Telegram on Sunday. “There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel.” SPRAVDI, Ukraine’s Centre for Strategic Communications, blamed Russia for the hack in a post on X. The raid alert app is used across Ukraine to warn people in real time of incoming Russian air attacks. A separate app, specifically for the Ukrainian capital, was working normally, according to Kyiv authorities. Hours later, early on Monday morning, Russia’s Emergencies Ministry said its mobile app had been hit by a “massive cyberattack”. items.blurb: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991.
items.text: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective C ora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa , meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare). items.headline: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
items.blurb: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
items.text: A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended. The localised ceasefire was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. While the truce had held since it was implemented last week, fighting had continued elsewhere. On Sunday evening, Ukraine's air alert system was apparently hacked, the country's air force said, warning of radiation over Kyiv - a reference to a possible nuclear attack. The Air Force message read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Some connections were restored on Sunday. Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said. items.headline: Tens of thousands build 108 Buddhist stupas for Bhutan ‘mindfulness’ city
items.blurb: Bhutan is building a 'mindfulness' city to drive economic growth and persuade more young people to stay.
items.text: Tens of thousands of volunteers have taken part in building 108 Buddhist stupas in Bhutan’s new “mindfulness” city, as the Himalayan kingdom embarks on an ambitious project to boost economic growth. The 15-metre-tall (50ft) stupas, sacred Buddhist monuments found across the Himalayas, were installed on Sunday along 12km (7.5 miles) of riverbank near the Indian border, at the site of the future Gelephu Mindfulness City. More than 40,000 volunteers participated in building the structures as “a physical form of prayer made permanent in stone and earth”, after starting work after midnight, officials said. The number 108 is sacred in Buddhism, widely practised in Bhutan. About 200,000 people attended the ceremony, or nearly a fourth of the population, officials told the AFP news agency. “I was worried that raising 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed,” Bhutan’s King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck said in a speech at the ceremony. The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked. Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide” . Nusseibeh, the UAE’s representative to the UN until 2024, has repeatedly reflected the UAE’s blanket denials of the accusations. items.headline: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat erupts
items.blurb: The move by Haley Stevens, who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, was called a "despicable betrayal" by one top Democrat.
items.text: A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote. Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday. "I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now." The move stunned many of Stevens' fellow Democrats who condemned her decision to break from the party and switch her support just two days before the election, with one calling it a "despicable betrayal". The public feud between Stevens, a centrist Democrat, and El-Sayed, who represents the party's left-wing, has boiled over in recent days. items.text: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups. “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP. items.text: Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire. In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy. In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties. The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information. Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel. items.headline: A fine balance: Reconciling large crowds and legacy lanes in Kolkata stampede aftermath
items.blurb: India’s fast-densifying cities are compressing more people into the same old streets, squares and festival routes.
items.text: A walk through north Kolkata is a lesson in anachronism. Its narrow, mazy lanes are flanked by cramped residential blocks and sprawling ancestral mansions in equal measure. Its neighbourhoods struggle to breathe and offer vast open spaces in the same breath. Historically home to prominent families such as the Tagores, Mullicks, Chatterjees and Seals, north Kolkata is where Durga Puja took on its modern, community-driven shape centuries ago. The neighbourhood’s pujas now draw hundreds of thousands of people every year, packing them into streets planned and built for far more modest numbers. On the evening of October 17, Saptami, families dressed traditionally for Durga Puja filled those lanes. Thousands filed through a narrow lane towards the Chorbagan Sarbojanin puja, one of the neighbourhood’s oldest pandals. By 7.40pm, the approach was packed. Then the skies opened. People outside pushed forward for shelter while those inside hesitated to step into the downpour. As the opposing flows jammed together, pressure built around the narrow exit. items.headline: Cyclone Murasu | Paddy farmers in Telangana fear crop damage amid high market prices
items.blurb: With soaked panicles delaying harvest, higher machine costs, and the need for extra drying and labor, growers warn that pre-flowering crops could suffer more, even as authorities issue alerts and supply protective tarpaulins to cushion the impact
items.text: The rain forecast under the impact of cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum) in various districts of Telangana from Monday to Wednesday (November 2 to 4) is giving jitters to farmers whose paddy and cotton crops are in various stages of cultivation. According to farmers, when rice panicles get soaked in rain and droops, machines used for harvesting paddy have to be hired for some more time, which results in spending more money. The soaked produce has to be dried, which may result in loss of some weight. Labour also need to be hired to channel water away from damaged paddy crops. And those in the pre-flowering stage might suffer greater damage. Currently, paddy crops are in various stages — depending on the time of sowing — ranging from harvest, nearing harvest and pre-flowering stage. items.headline: Households caught between LPG curbs, missing last-mile PNG connections
items.blurb: High connection costs and modest penalties discourage expansion into remote areas, while LPG restrictions leave some households without affordable fuel option.
items.text: HoHouseholds in far-flung areas even along gas pipelines face a double whammy: state-run gas agencies have stopped issuing new domestic liquefied petroleum gas ( LPG ) connections in certain areas since March, while piped natural gas (PNG) suppliers often find it cheaper to pay penalties than bear the high cost of laying pipelines for last-mile connections, people familiar with the matter said. The restriction has created difficulties for households that cannot access a PNG connection despite living in areas covered by a city gas distribution (CGD) licence, the people said. Meanwhile, CGD companies often do not extend pipelines to remote pockets within their authorised geographical areas because of the high cost of providing last-mile connectivity. This leaves some households dependent on more expensive 5kg and 10kg LPG cylinders. Some consumers also resort to buying domestic cylinders from the black market, they added. Distributors have been instructed not to issue new domestic LPG connections, which come with a 14.2kg cylinder, in areas where PNG is available or being made available, the people said, requesting anonymity. items.headline: Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu on alert as cyclone ‘Murasu’ looms
items.blurb: Heavy to very heavy rain is expected across parts of three states, while Odisha continues searching for people missing after Cyclone Arnab.
items.text: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Sunday directed officials to remain fully prepared for relief and rescue operations as another cyclone threat loomed over the state, while Tamil Nadu directed district collectors to remain on high alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next three days and Odisha stepped up preparedness in its southern region. This cyclone has been named ‘Murasu’ by India, meaning war drum. The previous cyclone to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast, neighbouring Odisha , was Arnab. It had wind speeds up to 150 kmph when it made landfall on October 28. “Another cyclone is approaching Andhra Pradesh and officials must remain fully prepared to undertake relief and rescue operations, as a severe cyclonic storm is expected to cross the coast near Bapatla on the morning of November 3,” Naidu said in a press release. The system is likely to bring moderate to heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy showers, over south and central coastal districts on November 2. items.blurb: Binance resumed customer withdrawals after a $6.3 billion cyber theft, reporting a $3.64 billion net outflow on Sunday. The exchange says it will cover the losses and has replenished 90% of the stolen funds. The FBI has attributed the attack to the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
items.text: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, on Sunday resumed withdrawal facility for its customers, days after it was hit by a massive cyber theft. Binance said that it had seen withdrawals of around $4.7 billion on Sunday, between 0600 GMT and 1530 GMT, and $1.01 billion in deposits. According to the company, the net outflow of $3.64 billion amounted to about 2.1 percent of the total assets it manages. The crypto exchange also played down the spike in withdrawals in the early hours, and said that volumes had declined and were stabilizing, while deposit volumes remained substantial. Co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao , aka CZ, also thanked Binance customers for their support. “2 hours after withdrawals resumed: 2.1% net outflow, with most occurring in the first couple of hours. Over $1 billion in flow, too. 98% choose to stay! Trust isn’t earned by what you say in good times. It’s earned by what you do in hard times. Thank you for your trust!,” CZ said in a post on X. items.headline: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
items.blurb: The exchange froze transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.
items.text: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week . The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack , which is said to be the largest hack in history. The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach, but that the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack. "Between 06:00 and 15:30 GMT on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," Binance posted on X. There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added. items.blurb: The e-commerce company is investing in local sourcing, demand planning and premium offerings to reduce wastage and strengthen its quick-commerce supply chain.
items.text: Bengaluru: Flipkart is betting that closer links with farmers and better demand planning can help it scale one of quick commerce's most operationally challenging categories: fresh produce. The e-commerce company is deepening partnerships with farmers and farmer producer organizations (FPOs), while investing in sourcing infrastructure and demand planning to reduce wastage on its quick-commerce platform Minutes. It also sees scope to expand premium offerings and introduce private labels, Kunal Gupta, senior vice-president of Flipkart and head of Flipkart Minutes, told Mint . “Our focus is on being closer to agricultural production centres so that we can source the freshest produce,” Gupta said. Flipkart works with 25 FPOs and more than 7,000 farmers directly across India. In Pune, one of Minutes' key markets, around 90% of its fruits and vegetables (FnV) procurement comes directly from farmers and farmer partners, Gupta said. Fresh produce offers margins of 20–40%, depending on the item, according to Satish Meena, analyst at market research firm Datum Intelligence. items.text: The startup plans to utilise the fresh proceeds towards financing the deployment of clean energy assets, strengthening the startup's tech stack and ramping up hiring The fresh capital gives Two Point O the war chest to enter the SME segment, expand across India and build an AUM of $100 Mn over the next couple of years The startup claims to have so far onboarded around 25–30 large customers and grown its AUM 1.5X sequentially in each of the last three quarters India’s clean energy transition is attracting significant capital, but much of it is flowing into utility-scale projects. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them. AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. items.headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.text: Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync. Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities. Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems. OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation , and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation , ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that. The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target. A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors.
